allocation_rules.cost_formula: sum((selected value - attribute minimum) * attribute weight) == budget
allocation_rules.package_rule: Every recommended package uses the same 12-point budget and follows the same limits as manual allocation.
allocation_rules.class_rule: A class recommends one package and one training profile but grants no hidden creation points or attribute bonus.
allocation_rules.preview_rule: You may change your class, package, guidance preference, or manual values until final confirmation.
allocation_rules.confirmation_rule: Confirmation locks your starting values. Later training adds to them without changing the creation budget.
allocation_rules.correction_rule: A future faction-headquarters story checkpoint is the planned explicit correction opportunity; this data does not silently reroll or infer a build.

attributes.name: Strength
attributes.summary: Direct attack pressure and carrying capacity.
effects: Comfortable carried bulk is max(6, Strength); throughout this legal range, each point adds +1 comfortable bulk.
Hard carried bulk is twice the comfortable limit; throughout this legal range, each point adds +2 hard bulk.
Strength does not currently add maximum health or flat weapon damage.

attributes.name: Agility
attributes.summary: Defense, evasion, withdrawal, and recovery speed at key thresholds.
effects: Each point adds +1 to opposed withdrawal escape.
Evade reaction is max(2, floor(Agility / 2) - armor penalty), so it normally improves every second Agility point.
Attack recovery is reduced by max(0, floor((Agility - 10) / 5)) seconds, subject to the existing 2-second hard floor; within this legal range, Agility 15 reaches the first 1-second reduction.

attributes.name: Perception
attributes.summary: Precision when aiming at a specific body location.
effects: The Character Foundation target formula for aimed attacks is max(4, 26 - Perception).
Across the legal 8–16 range, the aimed-attack defense penalty falls by exactly 1 for every Perception point: 18 at Perception 8 through 10 at Perception 16.
Legacy Perception 10 retains the prior 16-point aimed-attack penalty.
Perception does not change ordinary non-aimed attack math.

attributes.name: Combat Skill
attributes.summary: High-leverage general fighting fundamentals for offense, defense, and disengagement.
effects: Each point adds +2 to opposed withdrawal escape.
Combat Skill can indirectly improve damage or wound severity when its offense raises an endroll across an existing threshold; it is not a flat damage bonus.
Because one point affects three major contests, each creation point of Combat Skill costs 3 weighted points.

packages.name: General Foundation
packages.summary: A clear, forgiving balanced start suited to learning every core skill.

packages.name: Vanguard Foundation
packages.summary: Prioritizes direct offense and carrying capacity while keeping dependable general combat fundamentals.

packages.name: Sentinel Foundation
packages.summary: Balances strength and agility for a steady front line without spending creation points on precision.

packages.name: Skirmisher Foundation
packages.summary: Leans into defense and withdrawal while retaining strong general combat fundamentals.

packages.name: Field Operator Foundation
packages.summary: A flexible mix of mobility, usable precision, and enough strength for ordinary field loads.

packages.name: Recon Foundation
packages.summary: Favors mobility and aimed accuracy while accepting lighter carrying power and general combat training.

packages.name: Precision Foundation
packages.summary: Places the strongest emphasis on aimed attacks while preserving movement and combat competence.

packages.name: Technical Foundation
packages.summary: Keeps physical fundamentals even while reserving more of the equal budget for observation and precision.

aimed_attack_contract.legacy_compatibility: Perception 10 produces the existing 16-point aimed defense penalty.
aimed_attack_contract.player_promise: Every legal point of Perception has a visible one-point effect on aimed-attack difficulty.

tutorial.title: Guided Start
tutorial.description: An optional, reward-free orientation that teaches the smallest useful loop without assigning a faction, revealing later story turns, or blocking free exploration.
tutorial.reward_policy: Guided Start grants no exclusive item, experience, training point, class status, or faction status.

state_metadata.accept_transition: offered or skipped -> active at the first step
state_metadata.skip_transition: offered or active -> skipped with no penalty
state_metadata.completion_transition: active -> completed after the final verified event
state_metadata.resume_policy: GUIDE START may restart the orientation after a skip; completion remains recorded.
state_metadata.persistence: Your guidance status and current step stay with the character.

steps.description: Read the room and identify the obvious paths around you.
steps.why: LOOK is the fastest way to regain context after arriving, returning, or becoming disoriented.

steps.description: Review what you are carrying and what is already equipped.
steps.why: Your inventory affects available actions, protection, weapon profile, and encumbrance.

steps.description: Open the journal for a spoiler-safe summary of discoveries and progress.
steps.why: The journal preserves useful context without requiring you to remember every command or prior session.

steps.description: Leave the intake concourse and step into the Rain Market.
steps.why: Movement uses visible exits, and every newly reached room becomes part of your spatial memory.

steps.description: Say something in the Rain Market.
steps.why: The same command language supports social play as well as exploration and combat.
